blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 84th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2001 extended the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha and State Assembly seats until the first census published after 2026.
The original freeze was imposed by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 up to the year 2000 to encourage population control measures.
While the total number of seats remained fixed, the rationalization of constituency boundaries was permitted based on the 2001 Census under the 87th Amendment Act, 2003.
Post-2026 delimitation is expected to alter parliamentary representation significantly based on updated demographic figures across different states.

blocks.content: The freeze on the total number of seats in the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies continues until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published.

rows: Extend representation stability while enabling boundary rationalization

items: Questions frequently ask which Constitutional Amendment extended the Lok Sabha seat freeze to 2026 (Answer: 84th Amendment Act, 2001).
Note the distinction: The 84th Amendment initially used the 1991 Census for delimitation without changing seat counts, which was later updated to the 2001 Census by the 87th Amendment Act, 2003.
Remember that post-2026 delimitation depends on the publication of the census conducted after 2026, not the 2026 year itself.
